referenceStatus: Agent-drafted expectations; not human-approved ground truth.

topics.arrays: Arrays, lists, sequences, or subarrays are central to the task.
topics.strings: Processing, transforming, or comparing textual strings is central.
topics.numbers: Integer digits, representations, or numeric properties are central; merely using numeric values is insufficient.
topics.math: Arithmetic, algebra, number theory, combinatorics, or a mathematical relation is central.
topics.bit-manipulation: Binary representations or bit-level operations are central; binary search alone does not qualify.
topics.recursion: Recursion is explicitly requested or fundamental to the task; one possible recursive solution alone is insufficient.
topics.dynamic-programming: The task centrally involves optimizing over overlapping subproblems; explainable recurrence is a natural defining feature.
topics.sorting: Ordering or reordering data is a central requested operation; already sorted input alone is insufficient.
topics.searching: Finding a target, match, path, or boundary in a collection or search space is central.
topics.hash-maps: Maps, dictionaries, keyed lookup, frequency counting, or implementing a hash map is central.
topics.linked-lists: Linked nodes, list pointers, or linked-list operations are central.
topics.trees: A tree data structure or hierarchy of nodes is central; printing a pine-tree shape alone is insufficient.
topics.graphs: Vertices, edges, connectivity, or cycle structure is central, including implicit graphs when intrinsic to the task.
topics.stacks-queues: Stack or queue semantics, LIFO/FIFO behavior, or implementing these structures is central.
topics.matrices: A two-dimensional array, board, or grid and its cell relationships are central.
topics.intervals: Ranges, time spans, interval merging, or overlap between intervals is central.
topics.two-pointers: Coordinated pointer or index movement is a defining technique for the task, rather than an incidental possible implementation.
topics.sliding-window: Maintaining a contiguous moving window is a defining feature of the task.
topics.dates-times: Calendar dates, clocks, durations, or time calculations are central; identifiers containing a date are insufficient.
topics.geometry: Shapes, coordinates, distances, spatial relations, or geometric measurement are central.
topics.games: Rules or state of an actual game are central; a seasonal story alone is insufficient.
topics.parsing: Interpreting syntax, commands, encoded notation, or a structured textual format is central.
topics.regex: Regular expressions or regex matching are explicitly required or offered as a task variant; a prohibition on regex does not qualify.
topics.probability: Probability, random sampling, or randomized generation is central; the word random in a pointer or input description alone is insufficient.
topics.simulation: Modeling a sequence of state changes under explicit rules is central.
topics.data-structures: Designing or implementing a data structure is explicitly requested; merely receiving an array or string is insufficient.
